title: Debugging with AI check
instructions: Five questions on debugging with an AI partner.

questions.prompt: What should you include when you ask an assistant to help with a bug?
options: Only the words 'it does not work'
The full error message, the smallest code that shows the problem, what you expected and what happened
Your whole project and no description
Nothing, assistants can see your computer
questions.explanation: A precise report is the best input. Assistants cannot see anything you do not give them.

questions.prompt: What is the root cause of a bug?
options: The line where the error message appears
The underlying reason the program does the wrong thing
The last line you edited
The slowest part of the program
questions.explanation: The error shows where a problem became visible. The root cause is why it happened.

questions.prompt: An assistant suggests wrapping the failing code in try / except: pass. What is wrong with that?
options: Nothing, the error disappears
It hides the error instead of fixing it, so the bug remains and now nobody can see it
It makes the program slower
It is not valid Python
questions.explanation: Silencing an error is not a fix. The wrong behaviour is still there, with the evidence removed.

questions.prompt: What should you do before asking anyone for help with a bug?
options: Rewrite the program
Reproduce it with an input that fails every time, and shrink it if you can
Restart your computer
Delete the tests
questions.explanation: A bug you can repeat on a small example can be investigated and its fix can be checked.

questions.prompt: After applying a fix, what is the right check?
options: Assume it worked
Rerun the original failing input, rerun your other tests, and make sure you understand why it works
Ask the assistant if it worked
Delete the failing test
questions.explanation: Confirm the original failure is gone, confirm nothing else broke, and be able to explain the fix.

title: Fix the off-by-one
instructions:
`sum_to(n)` should return the sum of the whole numbers from 1 to `n`, so `sum_to(5)` is `15`. The version in the editor returns `10`. Find the **root cause** and fix it. Do not just add something to the result.

There is nothing to print. Your function is tested directly.

title: Order the debugging steps
instructions: Put the steps of a careful debugging session in the best order.
lines: Reproduce the bug with a small input
Read the error message and find the failing line
List possible causes and rank them
Test the most likely cause with a small experiment
Fix the cause and rerun the original failing case
